Equations and interpretation

Observed traffic

D = ΣqiΔt; Δt = 1/12 h; x = D/C (hours).

Tf = L/vf; P = t3 − t0.

wpeak = L/min(vi) − Tf.

w̄ = Σqi(L/vi − Tf)/Σqi.

Average speed = D L / ΣqiΔt(L/vi).

Recorded point speeds are treated as whole-link speed proxies. Delay is not clipped at zero.

QVDF predictions

P̂ = max(fdxn, x).

ŵpeak = Tf fpP̂s; w̄̂ = θ ŵpeak.

v̂t2 = L/(Tf + ŵpeak).

Fitted average speed = L/(Tf + w̄̂).

α = θ fp fds; β = ns. The reduced power law w̄̂ = Tfαxβ applies on the power branch.

Triangular FD and queue state

kc = C/vf; ω = C/(kj − kc).

ω is the positive magnitude of the backward wave; its signed propagation speed is −ω.

μ = D/P; μ̂ = D/P̂.

kq = kj − μ/ω; vq = μ/kq. Use μ̂ for the fitted state.

kj = 220 veh/mi/lane is an assumed closure constant. Observed and fitted state speeds share this FD; neither is an independent measured queue-speed target.

Capacity, S3 and comparison limits

C is the accepted detector S3 capacity, or the preserved profile 99.5th-percentile fallback. PeMS network metadata capacity divided by its lane count is shown only as a separate comparator.

S3 kc and vc describe the empirical S3 fit and differ from triangular kc = C/vf. Pre-S3 capacity is a profile estimate, not network metadata.

APE = 100 |fitted − observed| / |observed|. Zero reference denominators are undefined (—).

The separate CBI recovery-window flow is not the μ = D/P used in this queue-state calculation. Its QC flag is included only for provenance.

Parameter fits are by corridor, direction and period, with the saved corridor-wide fallback when period support is insufficient. Fit-source counts refer to the calibration cohort, not just these 137 retained emission cases. Profile dates identify average profiles; Arizona dates label months. These comparisons use fitted sample results, not an out-of-sample validation set.

Queue speed required to match the reference emissions

Each strategy selects one common queue speed for all four pollutants. CO₂ target matches CO₂ where physically attainable; Balanced four minimizes the mean squared relative error across CO₂, NOₓ, CO and HC, with equal weight ¼. Both are conditional diagnostics using O as the recorded-speed emission reference.

48 / 137episodes admit an exact CO₂ match
2 strategies × 137 episodessame queue speed used for all pollutants
Traffic predictions held fixedD, L, vf, mean and peak delay
Emission objective and physical constraint

Two-speed emission total M

t̄q(q) = vfw̄̂ / (vf − q).

t̄f(q) = Tf − q w̄̂ / (vf − q).

Mp(q) = D [t̄f(q) rp(vf) + t̄q(q) rp(q)].

q denotes the candidate queue speed vq here, not traffic flow. The original speed→VSP→mode lookup supplies rp.

Two diagnostic targets

CO₂: minimize |MCO₂(q)/OCO₂ − 1|.

Balanced: minimize J(q) = ¼ Σp[Mp(q)/Op − 1]².

Normalized RMSE = 100 √J (shown below). This is a balance across pollutants within one episode.

0 < q ≤ L/(Tf + ŵpeak) ensures nonnegative free-state time even at the peak delay.

Every lookup interval is solved separately. Rate jumps are retained; a jump crossing is never counted as a root. When multiple solutions tie, the one nearest the current fitted queue speed is selected. A rate-boundary limit is approached from one side and may have a nonzero residual. Superscript − or + identifies that side; use full-precision CSV values to reproduce the calculation.

Three backward FD calculations

ω is the positive backward-wave-speed magnitude (the γ in your question). Each calculation changes one quantity and holds the other two at their current values. μ₀ = D/P̂ is the fitted episode discharge.

1. Recover discharge

μ* = kj0 q ω₀ / (ω₀ + q).

Hold kj0, ω₀ fixed. The implied duration is P* = D/μ*. This generally differs from P̂; capacity stays fixed.

2. Recover wave speed

ω* = μ₀ q / (kj0 q − μ₀).

Hold μ₀, kj0 fixed. A finite positive solution exists only when kj0 q > μ₀.

3. Recover jam density

kj* = μ₀/q + μ₀/ω₀.

Hold μ₀, ω₀ fixed. The new wave/density pair implies C* = vfω*kj*/(vf + ω*), using whichever quantity changes.

A recovered μ that changes D/μ does not satisfy the original duration closure. A changed FD capacity changes D/C, so adopting it would require a new check of the QVDF predictions. These rows isolate the implications of each change; no fitted parameter or archived result is replaced.

Bounded combinations of jam density and backward-wave speed

Primary exploratory box: 150 ≤ kj ≤ 300 veh/mi/lane and 5 ≤ ω ≤ 20 mph. A second run lowers the wave-speed bound to 3 mph because some existing fitted wave speeds lie below 5 mph. These are explicit sensitivity assumptions, not universal limits or traffic-validated parameter estimates.

Keep the current discharge

For target q and fixed μ₀, exact pairs satisfy kj(ω) = μ₀/q + μ₀/ω.

The allowable ω interval is the intersection of this relation with the stated parameter box and physical speed bound.

Choose a candidate pair

First preserve the existing capacity wherever an exact target pair permits it. Otherwise select the pair with the closest implied capacity within the feasible interval.

If the target speed cannot be attained within the box, optimize the same emission objective over the attainable speeds. The achieved speed and remaining errors stay visible.

Published examples provide context for the sensitivity box: Laval and Daganzo use 150 veh/mi/lane and a 15 mph backward-wave magnitude; the GDOT I-285 study, Table 5 reports 150 veh/km and 20 km/h. Neither establishes the limits of this exploratory box.

Primary bounded combinations (CSV)Expanded 3–20 mph run (CSV)Sensitivity summaryBounds, sources and verification
